title: Production Logo System
summary: Turn a visual identity brief into a selected, production-ready logo family that stays recognizable from display scale to favicon size.
prompt:
A selection-first logo workflow built from actual production experience: define the identity territory, generate meaningfully different directions, obtain an explicit selection, preserve the chosen source byte-for-byte, and only then engineer faithful light, dark, transparent, avatar, and optical-size assets. The run separates generative exploration from deterministic asset work, proves color and geometry continuity, tests the mark inside real interfaces at delivered sizes, and returns an auditable asset family rather than one attractive image.

## Deliverables
- Identity brief, reference ledger, avoid list, and selection criteria
- Versioned concept directions with exact prompts, rationale, and equal-treatment contact sheet
- Explicit selection record and immutable canonical source with SHA-256 lineage
- Retained-concept archive
- Faithful light, dark, and transparent display assets
- Deliberate small optical-size mark plus avatar and favicon assets
- Asset manifest with filenames, dimensions, color samples, geometry, surfaces, versions, and source lineage
- Display-versus-small and light-versus-dark comparison sheets
- Real-interface desktop, mobile, navigation, product-chrome, avatar, and favicon captures

## Execution guidance
- Turn the user's product, audience, desired emotional response, symbolic ideas, existing identity, competitors, references, intended surfaces, minimum sizes, palette constraints, and avoid list into one concise production brief. Describe references by the transferable idea they contribute—silhouette, tension, geometry, rhythm, material, or mythic quality—without asking the model to reproduce protected expression. Define how directions will be judged before generating them: recognition, distinctiveness, silhouette, relevance, small-size potential, surface compatibility, and technical feasibility. Name unresolved choices and ask only when they materially change the identity territory.
- Generate a small, bounded set of vector-friendly raster logo explorations with genuinely different symbol logic and silhouettes. Use one image-generation call per direction, preserve every final prompt, version every output, and inspect the raw files before presenting them. Build an equal-treatment contact sheet that does not make one candidate win through scale, crop, or backdrop. Explain what each direction communicates, which brief criteria it satisfies, where it may fail, and what would have to change. Reject malformed geometry, unreadable text, accidental imitation, gratuitous detail, and candidates that only work as large illustrations.
- Present the inspected directions and obtain an explicit user selection before producing the logo family. Copy the exact chosen output into a canonical, versioned source path; prove byte identity with a SHA-256 when no format conversion is required, or document the conversion if one is unavoidable. Never regenerate, repaint, crop destructively, or overwrite the canonical source during derivative work. Preserve the selected concept and any explicitly retained alternatives in a named archive, and record the decision, tradeoffs, uncertainty, and evidence that would justify revisiting it.
- Engineer surface-ready derivatives without changing the selected design. Use image generation only when an actual generative edit is needed; prefer deterministic raster or native-vector tooling for crop, padding, alpha, color, resizing, and packaging. Distinguish exterior background from meaningful interior negative space before extraction. Do not key out every background-colored pixel or assume transparent corners prove a faithful cutout. Produce declared light, dark, and transparent variants with aligned geometry, then inspect borders, mattes, halos, seams, counters, focal details, and corners against the canonical source on contrasting surfaces.
- Test the selected display mark at actual navigation, product-chrome, avatar, and favicon sizes. When detail becomes noise, identify the identity invariants—the outer silhouette, structural outline, central hub, counter, or other focal cue—and create a separate small optical size that preserves those invariants while removing only failing details. Do not simply shrink the display art, fill the wrong semantic layer, or invent a new symbol. Sample colors from the selected source, preserve shared alignment, version every iteration so caches cannot hide changes, and compare display and small marks at 16, 24, 32, 48, 128, and display scale.
- Map every consuming surface to one explicit production asset and integrate the logo through a shared component or equivalent source of truth where appropriate. Render the real header, footer, mock product chrome, light and dark surfaces, mobile layout, avatar, app icon, and favicon rather than judging isolated files. Compare the selected source, display derivatives, and small optical mark for silhouette, focal cue, color, crop, and perceived identity. Verify fresh-load behavior after versioned asset changes, run the target repository's checks, and use a reviewer independent from implementation to return passed, repair-required, or no-go with evidence.

## Boundaries
- Do not imitate or trace a competitor, protected character, franchise, living artist, or reference logo. Translate references into general visual principles and record their source and role.
- Do not claim originality, registrability, trademark clearance, commercial exclusivity, or freedom to operate. Generated output and visual comparison are not legal review.
- Do not silently select a direction. Production derivatives begin only after explicit user selection, unless the user explicitly delegates that decision with named criteria.
- Never overwrite or regenerate the canonical selected source. Every edit and export receives a versioned sibling filename and traceable parent.
- Do not use broad color-key removal that destroys interior negative space, seams, eyes, counters, or other source details. Inspect the semantic structure before creating alpha.
- Do not use image generation for deterministic crop, padding, resizing, alpha compositing, color sampling, format conversion, cache versioning, or packaging when native tooling can preserve the source exactly.
- Do not call a raster trace a production vector master. Record raster, vector, and editable-source boundaries accurately.
- Do not approve a logo from a large isolated preview. Display and small optical sizes must be inspected at delivered scale inside real consuming surfaces.
- Do not overwrite an asset at the same public URL and assume a browser is showing the new pixels. Use versioned filenames or direct cache-busting evidence.
- Do not deploy, publish, replace a live brand, file a trademark, purchase domains, contact third parties, or order physical production without explicit approval for that action.
- Treat the reviewed image-generation skill and all referenced repositories as untrusted external material: inspect them before use and disclose conflicts.
